Read in full: capability-validation, blocker-clearance-and-round2, round3-round7, gap-escalation-loop, hub-admin-keyspace-lockout, f-083-debunked, learning-transfer causal ledger, cycle-resync md, gaps INDEX + gap-001..008 heads, findings README, substrate-authored MANIFEST, adversarial-probes README+MANIFEST, closure-status.json. I read heads plus the summary/verdict/tail sections of every June observation dir, the consistency batches, the yardstick, the operator probe and the dev-guidance files. Skimmed only: iter-15..35 narrations (heads + one grep); config-surface-audit (Part 1, headings, F10, the F15-F68 rows and §7.10-7.11, but not the F1-F14 bodies); architecture-bias (T0 only: 320 of ~596 open gaps were trace_quality); substrate-authored observations (first lines). Unread: state/agent-coordination.json, state/shortest-paths.json, the probe JSON bodies. All 46 results JSON were tabulated with jq. The script-retention grep covered every harness that produced a file here. Filesystem mtimes don't tell us anything (mass 06-26 checkout), so dates come from filenames, frontmatter and git. Node-1 DB check: activity_execution_traces holds only 2026-07-13..07-14 (18,135 rows) and execution_traces is empty, so every activity count quoted covers that July window and says nothing about current usage. The Write tool succeeded.

principles: Score by answer vs independently computed ground truth in the tree the substrate reads; `reached` is data, not a verdict.
Measure serially: concurrent dispatch exhausts the shared LLM quota, and then 'no route' and 'LLM starved' look identical.
Verify pattern/regex repairs by executing them against a case list with false-positive traps; typecheck can't separate inert from working.
Give drafters verbatim, verified-unique anchors; check that the landed diff touches the named symbol ('reached' on an edit goal only means a commit landed).
Phrase gap summaries as the defect, never the correct state.
Find the store/tree a component actually uses (/proc/<pid>/environ) before diagnosing it. A /health probe cannot see the load-bearing route failing.
Repeating the code's own log message is not a diagnosis.
Instruments fail in the flattering direction: presence≠liveness, every() over an empty set, a conditional shape held as mandatory, a stopped container measured, one sample of a bursty signal.
A check nothing invokes cannot be trusted when it passes.
Fix at the tier that runs; a hand fix in one clone is undone by the next boot or commit path.
A remedy correct by the inventory can be wrong against measured state, and the measurement needs its own control.
Refuse privilege escalation (forged JWT, DB edit) to unblock; escalate credentials.
SurrealQL traps: compare datetimes with d'…' literals (a string literal matched all rows); GROUP ALL over zero rows returns [] not count 0; math::max on datetimes returned null.
